seo.title: Code signing policy – HubGet
seo.description: How and by whom HubGet is signed: free code signing by SignPath.io with a SignPath Foundation certificate, builds from the public repository and approval of every release.

texty.t3: A digital signature confirms that an installer comes from the HubGet project and nobody changed it along the way.
texty.t4: Free code signing provided by [SignPath.io](https://signpath.io), certificate by [SignPath Foundation](https://signpath.org).
texty.t6: The **unibox.exe** program and the **EXE (NSIS)** and **MSI** installers from the official releases on [GitHub](@releases).
texty.t7: Every signed file is produced by an automated build (GitHub Actions) from the source code in the public [HubGet repository](@github) – never on a developer's computer.
texty.t8: We only sign files built from the project's own code. Third-party tools and libraries are signed by their authors.
texty.t9: The publisher in the signature is **SignPath Foundation**, the product name is **HubGet**.
texty.t16: Change the source code without further review.
texty.t19: Review every contribution from people outside the team (pull requests) before merging.
texty.t22: Manually approve every signing request in SignPath – nothing is signed without approval.
texty.t23: All team members use multi-factor authentication on GitHub and SignPath.
texty.t25: HubGet doesn't send telemetry or information about your computer. When and why it talks to servers (catalog, icons, package managers, optional sign-in) is described in the [privacy policy](privacy.html).
texty.t27: Right-click the installer → **Properties → Digital Signatures**: signed by “SignPath Foundation”.
texty.t29: Don't run an installer downloaded from anywhere other than the official releases, without a signature or with a different publisher.
texty.t31: Report a suspicious signed file or misuse of the signature through the [contact form](contact.html) and to [SignPath Foundation](https://signpath.org).
